_source: Customer_Import_FBDI_Sequence_Mapping_V2 2.xlsx (Tejaswi Medi, 29-Jul-2026; forwarded by Tejaswini 31-Jul-2026), reconciled 05-Aug-2026 against the V2.3 extraction in docs/incoming/customer_fbdi_column_order_V2.json (Customer_Import_FBDI_Sequence_Mapping_V2 3.xlsx, analyst 03-Aug-2026). The two carry the same content; see _reconciled.
_supersedes: Customer_Import_FBDI_Sequence_Mapping_V2 1.xlsx (30-Jul-2026). V2.3 (03-Aug) does not supersede this file — it was compared to it and found to say the same thing.
_reconciled: SESSION_HANDOFF 13.1b asked for this file to be REPLACED by the V2.3 extraction, and read as open for two days on the strength of the version numbers alone. The two were diffed on 05-Aug rather than one being assumed newer.

Identical across everything that decides a load: the same 15 interfaces in the same order, the same 15 CSV file names, 996 fbdi_order columns and 996 csv_order columns, and the same three interfaces where the CSV order differs from the worksheet order - HZ_IMP_ACCTSITES_T, HZ_IMP_ACCTSITEUSES_T and RA_CUSTOMER_PROFILES_INT_ALL.

ONE difference, and it is a defect in the extraction rather than a correction to this file. The V2.3 extraction's last csv_order entry for RA_CUSTOMER_PROFILES_INT_ALL reads 'Review Before Consolidated Billing,' with a trailing comma - the cell that sits immediately before the END terminator. Oracle's own bundled template settles it: CustomerImport_HZ_IMP__RA_CUSTOMER.xlsm, sheet RA_CUSTOMER_PROFILES_INT_ALL, header row 4, column 132 reads 'Review Before Consolidated Billing' with no comma. Adopting the extraction wholesale would have introduced a column name that matches nothing, on a headerless CSV where the mismatch is silent.

So the replacement in 13.1b item 1 is deliberately NOT done. The file is re-dated to 2026-08-03 because that is the date of the document its content agrees with; nothing about the column order changed, and the date is provenance here rather than precedence - customer_layout() reads this file directly and does not rank it against anything.
_why: Oracle's Customer Import workbook and the CSVs its macro generates DO NOT
share a column order. Three of the fifteen interfaces differ, and the
difference is silent: the column COUNT is identical, so a file built in sheet
order looks correct and loads every value into the wrong column.
HZ_IMP_ACCTSITES_T      — Account Number and Party Site Number move to the END
HZ_IMP_ACCTSITEUSES_T   — Account Number and Party Site Number move to the END
RA_CUSTOMER_PROFILES_INT_ALL — Party Original System/Reference, Credit Analyst,
Credit Review Cycle, Last/Next Review Date move
The generated CSVs are HEADERLESS, so position is the only thing carrying
meaning. Getting the order wrong on HZ_IMP_ACCTSITEUSES_T would load an
Account Number into the Account Site Source System column with no error.
